page: Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor. The instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage is bundled with a local 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present on this server type.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with the stress-ng single-core CPU test and Geekbench single-core score both placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is also a key strength, as evidenced by a strong PassMark memory score. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average tier. Data processing capabilities are balanced, with average performance in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing, though text processing registers as strong.

The server exhibits certain performance tradeoffs, particularly in LLM inference workloads. While prompt processing and text generation for small 135M models perform at average speeds, prompt processing for medium 7B models drops to the bottom 25% tier. Given the 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and the substantial 1280 GB NVMe SSD, this instance offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads. It is highly suitable for database hosting, memory-cached applications, text processing pipelines, and general-purpose web serving.
